signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Short Squeeze Risk
signals.text: JPY COT net short -124.6k (23.8% long) creates a massive squeeze risk as JPY outperformance accelerates—the pair closed Friday at 157.40, far below its SMA20 (162.34) and SMA50 (161.31). Extreme JPY strength (+2.979% 1W avg) overrides the +267bp OIS carry disadvantage as the market prices out USD dominance following intervention headlines. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) remains the catalyst for validating whether this month-end reversal toward the 157.95 SMA200 support is structural.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Resistance Breach
signals.text: GBP COT LF long +36.6k (67.3% long) warns of crowded-long exhaustion as the pair tests significant technical resistance after closing Friday at 1.3482. While the 1.3479 swing area was breached, the narrow -8bp OIS carry advantage for GBP offers limited fundamental protection if the US labor market data provides a hawkish surprise. The next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) is the catalyst for determining if the current bullish trend above the SMA200 (1.34) can be sustained against profit-taking pressure.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short Squeeze + Policy Divergence
signals.text: EUR COT net short -92.9k (30.7% long) sets up a high-probability squeeze risk after Eurozone inflation remained firm, pushing the pair to 1.1527. Firm inflation supports the ECB hike bias (next meeting 10 Sep), which contrasts with the Fed's hold stance and a -0.70% JPY real rate compared to EUR's +0.12%. The next ECB meeting (mkt: 51% hike priced) on 10 Sep is the catalyst for resolving the yield gap against the USD's +146bp OIS carry advantage.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Bearish Momentum + Crowded Short Divergence
signals.text: CAD COT net short -103.6k (16.3% long) diverges sharply from recent bearish price action as the pair closed Friday at 1.4017, breaking below key 4H trendlines. The extreme bearishness in CAD positioning suggests a massive contrarian reversal risk if the USD's +134bp OIS carry advantage fails to attract fresh buyers at current levels. The next BoC meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 9 Sep serves as the catalyst for validating the unfolding five-wave decline narrative.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Support + Retail Contrarian Risk
signals.text: NZD COT net short -30.6k is challenged by a strong ESI (+30.6) and an extreme retail short bias (78% short), favoring further upside from the 0.5877 close. Positive data surprises and the RBNZ's active hiking cycle (next meeting 2 Sep) support NZD strength despite a -1.56% negative real rate. The next RBNZ meeting (mkt: 98% hike priced) on 2 Sep is the catalyst to see if NZD can maintain its momentum above the SMA200 (0.5826).
